title: The Scope Was Complete
body:
[Plug & Prosper](https://smallloopworks.itch.io/plug-prosper) placed first overall in [AI Browser Game Jam 4](https://itch.io/jam/ai-jam-4/results), which I genuinely did not expect. It also ranked first for Theme, Graphics, Audio, and AI Usage, with Theme receiving its highest score at 4.9. Fun was its lowest placement at #11.

I played 29 of the 126 entries, and many felt more technically ambitious than any of my games. [Strait Across](https://moderndaedalus.itch.io/strait-across) was one of my personal favorites.

I submitted four different games, and their results did not match my expectations:

- **Plug & Prosper:** #1 overall with 10 ratings
- **Charge Knights:** #22 with 11 ratings
- **Charge Grid:** #39 with 7 ratings
- **Horizon Charge:** #79 with 8 ratings

In an early Discord poll, Charge Grid was the concept people found most interesting. It was also the project I expected to perform best, but it ultimately placed #39. These are small rating samples, so I would not treat the rankings as a universal measure of quality. The contrast is still useful: Plug & Prosper did not receive the most ratings, and the concept that sounded most interesting in advance was not the one that connected most strongly in the finished jam.

Plug & Prosper was the least ambitious of the four by scope, or at least that was how I saw it while working on it. Once I reached the point where I thought, “This game’s scope feels limited,” I mentally discounted it. Looking back, that feeling may actually have meant: **the scope was complete**. The idea was clearly defined, small enough to fully realize, and coherent enough that continuing to add things no longer felt necessary. I had confused “this does not need expansion” with “this lacks potential.”

There was a related lesson in the AI-assisted workflow. I had a clear picture of how the mechanics, presentation, and theme should fit together, and the project stayed within a technical surface I understood well. That let me direct the coding agents precisely, delegate fewer design decisions, and keep stronger control over the final result.

The result changes how I want to approach future jams. Technical ambition still matters, but a bounded idea that I understand and can finish coherently may be a better target than a larger system whose most important decisions remain unresolved.
